source_span: the August CPI and PPI data suggest that core PCE rose 0.27% last month, somewhat above pre-CPI expectations... we estimate that core PCE inflation has slowed to a 2.5% annualized pace over the last three months
source_chain: 16 of 18 FOMC participants signal one more hike by yearend, expected at the Oct 27-28 meeting, therefore the Fed delivers one final 25bp move and then holds flat, because the August print (core PCE +0.27% m/m) is consistent with core PCE having slowed to a 2.5% annualized pace over three months; invalidation is that pace failing to hold.
pulse_chain: Deutsche Bank's history of Fed underpricing (1994, 2022) plus 75bp still priced for hiking by June sets up Goldman's dovish one-hike-then-flat case (built on 2.5% core PCE) as the thing to test, therefore that case 'needs the data to start cooperating, and August did not' because the same 0.27% print is recast as hot and the annual rate is claimed to be 'still above 3% against a 2% target', compounded by a Saudi oil shock, therefore rates run higher for longer; invalidation is the 10-year (given as 4.99%) closing decisively above 5%, against BTIG's 4.92% flip level.
why: Goldman's own note uses the August 0.27% core-PCE print as evidence supporting its 2.5%-annualized disinflation call for a short hiking cycle, but the pulse cites that identical data point, paired with an unsourced 'still above 3%' annual figure, to claim the print undercuts Goldman's case — reversing the source's causal link between its own data and its own conclusion rather than compressing or rewording it.
